newsitem.title: USA: Zurich insurer in $2 billion deal with Scudder.
newsitem.headline: Zurich insurer in $2 billion deal with Scudder.

text.p: Swiss insurance firm Zurich Group and Scudder, Stevens & Clark Inc said early on Friday they have a definitive agreement to form a global investment firm in a deal valued at more than $2 billion.
The new firm, to be called Scudder Kemper Investments Inc, would have about $200 billion in assets under management.
Zurich will own about 69.5 percent of the new firm, while senior employees of privately held Scudder Kemper Investments will hold the remaining 30.5 percent.
The transaction involves a cash payment of $867 million and the contribution of Zurich's holding in Zurich Kemper Invesments Inc, a Chicago-based investment manager.
Scudder, Stevens & Clark president and chief executive Edmond Villani is to become chief executive of the new firm.

"This alliance strengthens our ability to meet the growing needs of U.S. investors and rising competition, and serves as a springboard for meeting the increasing demand for investment management services worldwide," Villani said in a statement.
The agreement had been approved by the boards of directors of both companies. It was expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997, the companies said.

"Globalization, deregulation and demographic trends are creating tremendous opportunities for companies that are prepared to respond," Zurich chairman and chief executive Rolf Hueppi said in a statement, adding that the combination "provides an ideal foundation to meet the changing needs of investors worldwide".
Zurich Kemper Investment has about $80 billion in assets under management, while Scudder has a $120 billion mutual fund and asset management operation.
The new firm is to be based in New York City. Friday, 27 June 1997 05:09:14 ENDS nN27194827
